risks.title: Failure of information systems and cybersecurity
risks.summary: ZBH relies heavily on sophisticated IT systems. A failure or cyberattack could disrupt operations, compromise customer data, and damage the company's reputation.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned at the beginning of Item 1A (first paragraph), strong language "could adversely affect", stable trend with strengthened governance (CISO with 30 years of experience, Audit Committee oversight), cybersecurity category = high regulatory and operational weight.

risks.title: Geographic concentration of critical operations
risks.summary: ZBH's core activities (R&D, manufacturing for knees/hips) are concentrated in Warsaw, Indiana. A local disruption (natural disaster, incident) could halt production of major products.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in Item 2 (Properties), moderate language "most significant", stable trend, major concentration in Warsaw (Indiana) for key R&D and manufacturing, potential impact on operational continuity.

risks.title: Dependence on new ERP system implementation
risks.summary: ZBH implemented a new ERP system that caused difficulties fulfilling customer orders in 2024. Risks of malfunctions persist and could affect production capacity and sales.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in Item 7 (MD&A) as cause of operational challenges in 2024, explicit language "operational challenges fulfilling customer orders", trend up (recent issues), documented financial impact (sales decline in 2024).

risks.title: Impairment charges and product discontinuations
risks.summary: ZBH recorded 170 million USD in charges related to discontinuing certain product lines. These impairments reduce profits and signal strategic or market missteps.
risks.score_rationale: Risk quantified in Item 7 (170 million USD inventory/instruments charges), direct language "intend to discontinue", trend new/up (non-recurring charge in 2025 not in 2024), direct impact on profitability.

risks.title: Pricing pressures and commercial competition
risks.summary: Hospitals, healthcare systems, and governments exert constant pressure to reduce prices. Although ZBH partially offsets this through internal initiatives, this pressure limits margin growth.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in Item 7 (Pricing Trends), moderate language "pricing pressure from local hospitals, health systems, and governmental healthcare cost containment efforts", trend stable/chronic, impact partially offset but persistent.

risks.title: Risks related to recent acquisitions and integration
risks.summary: ZBH acquired Paragon 28 (April 2025) and Monogram (October 2025), generating integration costs and increased debt. Successful integration of these entities is critical to justify the investments.
risks.score_rationale: Risk documented in Item 7 (acquisitions of Paragon 28 and Monogram), explicit language "acquisition-related costs and higher interest expense", trend new (two acquisitions in 2025), measurable financial impact (decline in net profits).

risks.title: Currency volatility and international exposure
risks.summary: ZBH generates 42% of its sales internationally and is affected by exchange rate fluctuations. Although 2025 benefited from a positive effect, future variations could reduce revenues converted into USD.
risks.score_rationale: Risk implicit in Item 7 (Foreign Currency Exchange Rates), neutral language "positive effect of 0.8 percent", trend stable (favorable effect in 2025 but expected volatility), 42% of sales international (3.5 Bn USD / 8.2 Bn USD).

risks.title: Deterioration in stock performance and value creation
risks.summary: ZBH stock has lost 37% of its value since 2020 while the S&P 500 gained 96%. This persistent underperformance erodes investor confidence and complicates future capital raising.
risks.score_rationale: Risk visible in Item 5 (Market for Registrant's Common Equity), factual data: ZBH stock -37% since 2020 vs S&P 500 +96%, trend down (continuous decline 2020-2025), impact on investor confidence and financing capacity.

ai_positioning.summary: ZBH does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K report. The information provided focuses primarily on financial aspects, acquisitions, and company operations without addressing emerging technologies such as AI.
